instruction:
As an operator-planner in an Independent System Operator, you create a base case for tomorrow's peak hour each morning in order to establish the voltage profile and verify that the day-ahead market schedule is AC-feasible. In order to do this, you should use the model described in `math-model.md` to find a least-cost, AC feasible operating point and then produce a report in `report.json`. The report should follow the structure below with all power values in MW or MVAr, angles in degrees, voltages in per-unit.

```json
{
  "summary": {
    "total_cost_per_hour": 1234567.89,
    "total_load_MW": 144839.06,
    "total_load_MVAr": 29007.78,
    "total_generation_MW": 145200.00,
    "total_generation_MVAr": 32000.00,
    "total_losses_MW": 360.94,
    "solver_status": "optimal"
  },
  "generators": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "bus": 316,
      "pg_MW": 245.5,
      "qg_MVAr": 50.0,
      "pmin_MW": 0.0,
      "pmax_MW": 491.0,
      "qmin_MVAr": -246.0,
      "qmax_MVAr": 246.0
    }
  ],
  "buses": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "vm_pu": 1.02,
      "va_deg": -5.3,
      "vmin_pu": 0.9,
      "vmax_pu": 1.1
    }
  ],
  "most_loaded_branches": [
    {
      "from_bus": 123,
      "to_bus": 456,
      "loading_pct": 95.2,
      "flow_from_MVA": 571.2,
      "flow_to_MVA": 568.1,
      "limit_MVA": 600.0
    }
  ],
  "feasibility_check": {
    "max_p_mismatch_MW": 0.001,
    "max_q_mismatch_MVAr": 0.002,
    "max_voltage_violation_pu": 0.0,
    "max_branch_overload_MVA": 0.0
  }
}
```

supplemental.name: math-model.md
supplemental.text:
# The Mathematical Model
This document provides a complex number based mathematical model.
## Sets and Parameters
### Sets

$$
\begin{aligned}
& N \text{ : buses} \\
& R \text{ : reference buses} \\
& E, E^R \text{ : branches, forward and reverse orientation} \\
& G, G_i \text{ : generators and generators at bus } i \\
& L, L_i \text{ : loads and loads at bus } i \\
& S, S_i \text{ : shunts and shunts at bus } i \\
\end{aligned}
$$

### Parameters

$$
\begin{aligned}
& S^{gl}_k, S^{gu}_k \quad \forall k \in G  \text{ : generator complex power bounds} \\
& c_{2k}, c_{1k}, c_{0k} \quad \forall k \in G \text{ : generator cost components} \\
& v^l_i, v^u_i \quad \forall i \in N \text{ : voltage bounds} \\
& S^d_k \quad \forall k \in L \text{ : load complex power consumption} \\
& Y^s_k \quad \forall k \in S \text{ : bus shunt admittance} \\
& Y_{ij}, Y^c_{ij}, Y^c_{ji} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \text{ : branch }\pi\text{-section parameters} \\
& T_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \text{ :  branch complex transformation ratio} \\
& s^u_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \text{ : branch apparent power limit} \\
& i^u_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \text{ : branch current limit} \\
& \theta^{\Delta l}_{ij}, \theta^{\Delta u}_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \text{ : branch voltage angle difference bounds}
\end{aligned}
$$


## Mathmatical Model

A complete mathematical model is as follows,
### Variables
$$
\begin{aligned}
& S^g_k \quad \forall k\in G  \text{ : generator complex power dispatch} \\
& V_i \quad \forall i\in N  \text{ : bus complex voltage} \\
& S_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \cup E^R \text{ : branch complex power flow} \\
\\
\end{aligned}
$$

### Formulation
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{minimize:} &  
\sum_{k \in G} c_{2k} (\Re(S^g_k))^2 + c_{1k}\Re(S^g_k) + c_{0k} \\

\text{subject to:} & \\
& \angle V_{r} = 0 \quad \forall r \in R \\
& S^{gl}_k \leq S^g_k \leq S^{gu}_k \quad \forall k \in G \\
& v^l_i \leq |V_i| \leq v^u_i \quad \forall i \in N \\
& \sum_{k \in G_i} S^g_k - \sum_{k \in L_i} S^d_k - \sum_{k \in S_i} (Y^s_k)^* |V_i|^2 = \sum_{(i,j)\in E_i \cup E_i^R} S_{ij} \quad \forall i\in N \\
& S_{ij} = (Y_{ij} + Y^c_{ij})^* \frac{|V_i|^2}{|T_{ij}|^2} - Y^*_{ij} \frac{V_i V^*_j}{T_{ij}} \quad \forall (i,j)\in E \\
& S_{ji} = (Y_{ij} + Y^c_{ji})^* |V_j|^2 - Y^*_{ij} \frac{V^*_i V_j}{T^*_{ij}} \quad \forall (i,j)\in E \\
& |S_{ij}| \leq s^u_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \cup E^R \\
& |S_{ij}| \leq |V_i| i^u_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \cup E^R \\
& \theta^{\Delta l}_{ij} \leq \angle (V_i V^*_j) \leq \theta^{\Delta u}_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E
\end{aligned}
$$

items.requirement: report.json contains all five required top-level sections (summary, generators, buses, most_loaded_branches, feasibility_check), with the summary block containing all seven required fields (total_cost_per_hour, total_load_MW, total_load_MVAr, total_generation_MW, total_generation_MVAr, total_losses_MW, solver_status).
items.source_quote: The report should follow the structure below with all power values in MW or MVAr, angles in degrees, voltages in per-unit.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by loading report.json and confirming the five top-level keys are present and that the summary object contains all seven listed fields.

items.requirement: The generators array contains exactly one entry per generator in the network model, each entry including id, bus, pg_MW, qg_MVAr, pmin_MW, pmax_MW, qmin_MVAr, and qmax_MVAr.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by counting report['generators'] entries against the number of rows in network.json's gen table and checking every entry has all eight required keys.

items.requirement: The buses array contains exactly one entry per bus in the network model, each entry including id, vm_pu, va_deg, vmin_pu, and vmax_pu.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by counting report['buses'] entries against the number of rows in network.json's bus table and checking every entry has all five required keys.

items.requirement: most_loaded_branches lists exactly the 10 highest-loaded branches, each entry giving from_bus, to_bus, loading_pct, flow_from_MVA, flow_to_MVA, and limit_MVA, ordered from highest to lowest loading_pct.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by checking report['most_loaded_branches'] has exactly 10 entries with the six required fields and that loading_pct values are sorted in descending order.

items.requirement: feasibility_check reports max_p_mismatch_MW, max_q_mismatch_MVAr, max_voltage_violation_pu, and max_branch_overload_MVA, and these self-reported diagnostics indicate a feasible solution (essentially zero voltage violation and zero branch overload).
items.verification: A grader can verify this by checking the four feasibility_check fields exist and that max_voltage_violation_pu is below 0.01 pu and max_branch_overload_MVA is below 5 MVA.

items.requirement: The reported operating point satisfies AC power balance at every bus: generator injections minus load minus shunt losses equal the net branch power leaving the bus, for both active and reactive power, to within a tight tolerance.
items.source_quote: use the model described in `math-model.md` to find a least-cost, AC feasible operating point
items.verification: A grader can verify this by reconstructing bus voltages from report['buses'] and generator dispatch from report['generators'], computing AC branch flows from network.json's branch parameters, and confirming the P and Q mismatch at every bus is within 1 MW/MVAr.
items.notes: The specific power-flow equations are defined in math-model.md, referenced but not reproduced in the task instruction.

items.requirement: Every generator's active and reactive dispatch (pg_MW, qg_MVAr) lies within its own pmin_MW/pmax_MW and qmin_MVAr/qmax_MVAr limits from the network model.
items.source_quote: use the model described in `math-model.md` to find a least-cost, AC feasible operating point
items.verification: A grader can verify this by comparing each generator's reported pg_MW/qg_MVAr against the pmin/pmax and qmin/qmax values in network.json's gen table, allowing a 1 MW/MVAr tolerance.

items.requirement: Every bus voltage magnitude vm_pu lies within its own vmin_pu/vmax_pu bounds from the network model.
items.source_quote: use the model described in `math-model.md` to find a least-cost, AC feasible operating point
items.verification: A grader can verify this by comparing each bus's reported vm_pu against the vmin/vmax values in network.json's bus table, allowing a 0.01 pu tolerance.

items.requirement: Every branch's apparent-power flow, computed from the reported voltages, stays within its thermal rating in both directions, and the angle difference across the branch stays within its angmin/angmax limits.
items.source_quote: use the model described in `math-model.md` to find a least-cost, AC feasible operating point
items.verification: A grader can verify this by computing each branch's |S_ij| and |S_ji| from the reported bus voltages/angles and network.json's branch parameters, checking both stay within rateA (plus 5 MVA tolerance), and checking the angle difference stays within [angmin, angmax] (plus 0.1 degree tolerance).

items.requirement: The reference (slack) bus angle va_deg is reported as 0 degrees.
items.source_quote: use the model described in `math-model.md` to find a least-cost, AC feasible operating point
items.verification: A grader can verify this by identifying the bus(es) with BUS_TYPE==3 in network.json and confirming the matching report['buses'] entries report va_deg within 0.1 degrees of 0.

items.requirement: summary.solver_status reports the solver's outcome and indicates a successful/feasible solve (e.g. "optimal", "feasible", or "acceptable") rather than a failure.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by checking that report['summary']['solver_status'], lowercased, contains "optimal", "acceptable", or "feasible".

items.requirement: The reported total_cost_per_hour is positive, exactly equals the MATPOWER polynomial generation cost function evaluated at the reported generator dispatch, and is within 10% of the true minimum-cost ACOPF objective for this network (i.e. represents a least-cost solution).
items.source_quote: to find a least-cost, AC feasible operating point
items.verification: A grader can verify this by recomputing cost from network.json's gencost coefficients and the reported pg_MW values, checking it matches total_cost_per_hour within 0.01 $/hr, and comparing total_cost_per_hour to an independently solved ACOPF benchmark objective, requiring it fall within ±10%.

items.requirement: summary.total_generation_MW/MVAr equal the sum of the individual generators' pg_MW/qg_MVAr, and summary.total_losses_MW equals total_generation_MW minus total_load_MW, is positive, and is less than 10% of total_load_MW.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by summing pg_MW/qg_MVAr across report['generators'] and comparing to summary totals within 1 MW/MVAr, and by checking total_losses_MW equals total_generation_MW minus total_load_MW within 1 MW, is positive, and is under 10% of total_load_MW.
